chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid narrated to me in his book, Al-Jami', from Abul Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:
When you wish to bid farewell to the grave of the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him), say:
Peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. I entrust you to Allah and ask Him to protect you, and I convey peace to you.
We have believed with a true belief in Allah and the Messenger [the Messengers and what they brought and invited to and indicated - so record us among the witnesses.
O Allah, do not let this be the last occasion of my visiting him. If You cause me to die before that, then I testify in my death upon what I testified in my life.
I testify that you are the Imams - and name them one after another.
And I testify that whoever killed them and fought them were polytheists, and whoever opposed them and opposed their knowledge is in the lowest depth of Hell.
And I testify that whoever fought them are our enemies and we are free from them, and that they are the party of Satan.
And upon whoever killed them is the curse of Allah, the angels, and all people, and whoever participated with them.
O Allah, I ask You after prayer and peace to send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad.
And do not let it be the last occasion of my visiting him, and if You make it so, then resurrect me with these named Imams.
O Allah, make our hearts humble for them through obedience, sincerity, love, and good support.

key_terms.زِيَارَةٌ: Visitation (to the graves of the Imams)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to recite when bidding farewell to the grave of Imam Ali (a.s.)?
ai.summary: This du'a from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* encapsulates the Shia doctrine of *Tawalli* (affinity) and *Tabarri* (disaffinity) by explicitly linking personal faith to the Imams, declaring their enemies as *Ashab al-Kahf* (companions of the cave/enemies of God), and invoking curses upon those who oppose them. It concludes with a profound eschatological hope for resurrection (*Hashr*) alongside the Imams, reflecting the Shia belief in their intercessory role and the continuity of spiritual allegiance beyond death.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 1. Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan ibn Aḥmad ibn Walīd narrated in his book, Al-Jāmi’, that: Abul Ḥasan (Imam Kāżim (a.s.)) said:
When you want to bid farewell to the grave of the Commander of the Believers (a.s.), recite (the following):
Salām to you and (may) Allāh’s Mercy and Blessings be upon you. I entrust you to Allāh and I ask Allāh to protect you. I extend my Salām to you.
We believe in Allāh, His messengers, in that which they brought with them, and in that to which they invited and guided (the people). Therefore, include us among those who testify.

O Allāh! Do not let this be the last time I come to his Ziyārah. If You take my life before I come to his Ziyārah again, then surely I will testify after my death to that which I testified during my life.
I testify that you are the Imams – and name the Imams one after another.
And I testify that those who killed them and those who fought them were polytheists and that those who oppose their words and their knowledge are in the lowest levels of Hell.
I testify that those who fought them are our enemies and we dissociate ourselves from them, and that they are the party of Shayťān.
(May) Allāh’s curse, the curse of the angels, and (the curse of) all of the people be upon those who killed them, those who participated in their killing, and those who were pleased with it.
O Allāh! After having established prayers and having said Salām (to the Imams (a.s.)), I ask You to send Your Blessing on Muḥammad and his family.
Do not let this be the last time I come to his Ziyārah, and if it is, then resurrect me with the mentioned Imams.
O Allāh! Humble our hearts toward them through our obedience and sincerity (to them), our love for them, and our support for them .
